Each roving is tension controlled by a spring and the opening through which the rovings exit are shown in the image on the right. 11 Fiber weight consistency is critical for producing uniform quality sheet molding compound (SMC). Studies were conducted to evaluate weight consistency using a hexagonal collection tray placed directly under the cutting module to collect 160 g of chopped fiber at set time intervals. The line was operated at a speed of 20 ft/min with a programmed fiber length of 1 inch. During testing, specific fiber length, conveyor speed, and collection time frames were dialed in to estimate the expected fiber mass within each interval. The collected samples were weighed across multiple drops to verify consistency and confirm fiber weight fraction (Wf). This investigation examined both volume fraction consistency at the point of cutting and material migration through the line to the final product. As shown in Figure 11, results indicate a consistent fiber weight fraction for 1- inch chopped fibers at the target collection weight of 160 g. Figure 11. Illustration of uniform cutting of the glass fiber rovings. 16 of the 18 ends are fed in this run 12 The textile grade carbon fiber (TCF) is a wide tow fiber with 330 to 450k filaments and very different from a standard tow 12k, 24k or 50k commercial fiber. There is no SMC history with this fiber form and this was one of the key developments in this work. Two modules were designed and fabricated for TCF chopping, one for the 330k Montefibre precursor based TCF and one for the 450k Kaltex precursor based TCF. Figure 12 illustrates the cutting module for the 450k tow, which has only two feeds to produce the 18” wide SMC as can be seen from the figure. Each 450k tow feeds through one of the ends. Several cutting challenges had to be overcome to obtain uniform fiber length TCF. Figure 13 illustrates the cutting module for the 300k Montefibre precursor based TCF. This module has 5 feed ends of the 300k fibers to produce the 18” wide SMC. In each of these cases trials were run to evaluate the cutting uniformity, feed and fiber length consistency. Figure 12.
